title: Calling, messaging, rescheduling
title_target: โทรหา นัดใหม่ — Thoo hǎa, nát mài
goal: Make and answer phone calls, leave a message, set up an appointment and change it — including how to apologize for being late without making the other person feel slighted.

dialogs.title: บทสนทนา — Calling the office, then rescheduling
dialogs.intro: Budi calls Nok's office. Notice that Thai phone calls have an opening and a closing that are almost fixed — memorize both and everything in between gets much easier.

lines.text: [สวัสดี|Sà-wàt-dii][ค่ะ|khâ] [บริษัท|Baw-rí-sàt][ลิงกัว|Ling-kua][ค่ะ|khâ]

lines.text: [สวัสดี|Sà-wàt-dii][ครับ|khráp] [ขอ|Khǎaw][สาย|sǎai][คุณ|khun][นก|Nók][หน่อย|nàwy][ครับ|khráp]

lines.text: [รอ|Raw][สักครู่|sàk-khrûu][นะ|ná][คะ|khá] … [ตอนนี้|Tawn-níi][คุณ|khun][นก|Nók][ไม่|mâi][อยู่|yùu][ค่ะ|khâ] [ติด|Tìt][ประชุม|prà-chum][ค่ะ|khâ]

lines.text: [ได้|Dâai][ค่ะ|khâ] [ขอ|Khǎaw][ทราบ|sâap][ชื่อ|chûue][ด้วย|dûai][ค่ะ|khâ]

lines.speaker: บูดี:
lines.text: [ผม|Phǒm][บูดี|Buu-dii][ครับ|khráp] [ช่วย|Chûai][บอก|bàwk][ว่า|wâa][พรุ่งนี้|phrûng-níi][ผม|phǒm][ไป|pai][ไม่|mâi][ได้|dâai][ครับ|khráp]

lines.text: [ค่ะ|Khâ] [แล้ว|Láaeo][จะ|jà][นัด|nát][ใหม่|mài][เมื่อไหร่|mûea-rài][คะ|khá]

lines.id: Would Friday at 2 p.m. work? If that's not convenient, could she call me back?
lines.literal: day — Friday — afternoon — two — o'clock — can — (question) — (polite)? if — not — convenient — trouble — phone — back — (polite).

lines.text: [รับทราบ|Ráp-sâap][ค่ะ|khâ] [เดี๋ยว|Dǐao][แจ้ง|jâaeng][ให้|hâi][ค่ะ|khâ]

lines.text: [ขอบคุณ|Khàwp-khun][มาก|mâak][ครับ|khráp] [สวัสดี|Sà-wàt-dii][ครับ|khráp]

lines.speaker: นก:
lines.text: [ฮัลโหล|Han-lǒo] [พี่|phîi][บูดี|Buu-dii][คะ|khá] [เพิ่ง|Phôeng][เห็น|hěn][ข้อความ|khâw-khwaam][ค่ะ|khâ] [ศุกร์|Sùk][บ่าย|bàai][สอง|sǎawng][ว่าง|wâang][ค่ะ|khâ]
lines.id: Hello, Phi Budi. I just saw your message. I'm free Friday at two.
lines.literal: hello — older-sibling — Budi — (polite). just — see — message — (polite). Friday — afternoon — two — free — (polite).

lines.speaker: บูดี:
lines.text: [ขอโทษ|Khǎaw-thôot][ที่|thîi][เลื่อน|lûuean][นะ|ná][ครับ|khráp] [เจอ|Joee][กัน|kan][ที่|thîi][เดิม|dooem][ครับ|khráp]
lines.id: Sorry for postponing. See you at the usual place.
lines.literal: sorry — that — shift — okay — (polite). meet — together — at — original — (polite).

notes: **ขอสาย… หน่อยครับ/ค่ะ is the standard phrase for "may I speak to…".** The word *สาย sǎai* here means "phone line" — yet another meaning, different from the *สาย* that means "late" (unit 7).

**ติดประชุม tìt prà-chum means "in a meeting, can't be disturbed".** The word *ติด tìt* (stuck) forms many excuses: *ติดธุระ* (tied up with something), *ติดงาน* (busy at work), *ติดประชุม*, and of course *รถติด* (traffic jam) from unit 7.

**ฝากข้อความ fàak khâw-khwaam = leave a message.** The word *ฝาก fàak* (entrust) is very handy: *ฝากบอก…หน่อย* (please pass on to…), *ฝากซื้อ…หน่อย* (could you pick up … for me). The last one is something Thai people say every day to a coworker heading out for lunch.

**ทราบ sâap is the respectful form of รู้ rúu (know)**, and you'll hear it on office phones, at airports, and in announcements. You don't need to use it yourself; just recognize it. The form *รับทราบ ráp-sâap* means "noted, understood" — the standard reply at work.

**นัด nát means "appointment", both as a noun and a verb.** *นัดใหม่* (reschedule), *มีนัด* (have an appointment), *ผิดนัด phìt nát* (miss an appointment). ⚠️ Don't confuse it with *สัญญา sǎn-yaa*, which means a promise or a contract.

**เลื่อน lûuean means "to shift, to postpone".** *ขอเลื่อนนัดได้ไหม* (could we move the appointment?). The firmer form: *ยกเลิก yók-lôoek* (cancel). In Thailand, postponing is much preferred to canceling — it keeps the relationship open.
**ขอโทษที่… khǎaw-thôot thîi … means "sorry for…".** *ขอโทษที่เลื่อน* (sorry for postponing), *ขอโทษที่มาสาย* (sorry I'm late), *ขอโทษที่โทรมาดึก* (sorry for calling so late).
**ที่เดิม thîi dooem = "the usual place".** The word *เดิม dooem* means "original, as before": *ราคาเดิม* (the original price), *ที่เดิม*, *เวลาเดิม* (the usual time).

sections.title: LINE: how Thai people really message

blocks.text: In Thailand, everyday messaging happens almost entirely on **LINE**, not WhatsApp or SMS. Swapping contacts means swapping LINE, and the question goes: *ขอไลน์ได้ไหมครับ/คะ khǎaw lai dâai mǎi* — could I get your LINE?

blocks.title: Why 555 means laughing
items: The number **5** in Thai is read *ห้า hâa*. So **555** reads *hâa-hâa-hâa* — and that's how Thai people write laughter, just like "hahaha" or "lol".
The longer the string, the funnier: *5555555*. If you get a message full of fives, you've made someone laugh — it's not a phone number.
Other casual spellings you'll see: *ค่า* and *คับ* (cutesy forms of *ค่ะ* and *ครับ*), *จ้า jâa* (a warm "yes"), and *นะคะ/นะครับ* written out in full as an extra touch of politeness.
**Don't call out of the blue about something you could write.** In Thailand, an unannounced call feels somewhat urgent; a LINE message is preferred for routine matters.
**If you must call outside working hours**, open with *ขอโทษที่โทรมาดึกนะครับ/คะ* (sorry for calling so late) — that opening line takes care of all the politeness in one go.
**Reply to messages even if you can't answer yet.** *รับทราบครับ/ค่ะ* (noted) or *เดี๋ยวตอบนะครับ/คะ* (I'll get back to you) is enough — staying silent too long comes across as rude.
**If you're the one at fault**, don't explain at length. *ขอโทษครับ/ค่ะ* followed by a clear fix is valued far more than a detailed excuse.

blocks.title: Asking favors by message
items: **ฝากซื้อ…หน่อยได้ไหมครับ/คะ** — could you pick up … for me?
**ช่วยส่งไฟล์ให้หน่อยได้ไหมครับ/คะ** *chûai sòng fai hâi nàwy dâai mǎi* — could you send me the file?
**รบกวนด้วยนะครับ/คะ** — sorry for the trouble. Added to the end of any request, this makes the whole message sound much softer.
"May I speak to Khun Nok?" → ขอ____คุณนกหน่อยครับ
"One moment, please" → รอ____นะคะ
"Could I leave a message?" → ____ข้อความได้ไหมครับ
"Please call back" → รบกวน____ด้วยครับ
"Could we move it?" → ขอ____ได้ไหมคะ
"Sorry I'm late" → ขอโทษที่____ครับ
